subject: Renewal discussion: premium SLA, latency SLO tightening and burst capacity
messages:
From: Ethan Holt <ethan.holt@pulsepay.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 29 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal conversation + premium SLA request

Karthik,

We’ll be renewing with Redwood in September and the exec team has asked whether we can upgrade to a premium SLA for the next term. Two specific asks from our infra team:

- Tighten P99 latency SLO to <= 160ms for the core payments route (current commitment is 220ms).
- Guaranteed burst capacity: 2x baseline throughput for 6 hours/day during peak events (Black Friday-style windows).

We’re prepared to move to a 12-month committed spend if we can get a firm SLO and an addendum that specifies the burst behavior and credits if SLOs are missed. Can you put together a proposal and indicative uplift? We’ll need this for our internal renewal packet next week.

Also looping procurement later (procure@pulsepay.com).

Best,
Ethan
Ethan Holt
Head of Engineering, PulsePay
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Ethan Holt <ethan.holt@pulsepay.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 29 Jul 2025 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation + premium SLA request

Ethan — thanks for the clear ask. High level response: we can support a tightened P99 SLO to 160ms for the core payments route with a few conditions (seq len distribution and request mix as discussed in onboarding). For burst capacity we can offer a dedicated burst pool that scales to 2x baseline for defined windows.

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll send an SLA addendum draft (SLA_Addendum_PulsePay_v2.pdf) with explicit SLO language, measurement windows, and credit calculations.
- Grace (CC’d) will model the uplift and show impact on unit economics; expect a ballpark uplift of ~20–25% for the dedicated burst + tightened SLO.
- Marissa will scope a short pilot to validate tail latency at your peak mix before we finalize the addendum.

Can you confirm the most likely peak windows (dates/times) and whether the burst guarantee needs to be regional (US-only) or global?

Thanks,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 30 Jul 2025 08:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: PulsePay uplift and modelling

Quick internal note — I pulled PulsePay’s Q2 usage (attached: PulsePay_Q2_usage_summary.csv) and ran a couple of scenarios:

- Option A (12m commit, premium SLA + burst pool): +22% ARR uplift vs current consumption; includes a reserved baseline and 2x burst available up to 6 hours/day for 12 defined days per quarter.
- Option B (12m commit, SLO tightening only): +12% ARR uplift; no dedicated burst but priority routing.
- Credits: propose 4x monthly pro-rated credit for an SLO miss per impacted route (capped).

Caveats: the 160ms P99 is realistic if we require PulsePay to run the recommended request shaping (prefix caching + KV cache sizing) and we limit max seq to 1.5x current median during bursts. Pilot data will validate.

I’ll draft the pricing table and send to Kar for inclusion in the addendum. Rafael — can you review the credit calc and operational impact?

—Grace
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Ethan Holt <ethan.holt@pulsepay.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 31 Jul 2025 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation + premium SLA request

Ethan — I can run a short 2-week pilot that recreates your peak mix against our dedicated burst pool. The pilot plan:

1) Snapshot: mirror your Q2 request mix (we’ll ask for a representative Replay trace, 3–4 sample days).
2) Pilot window: 10 business days, with 2 synthetic peak windows (3 hours each) to validate tail.
3) Success criteria: P99 <= 160ms across pilot peak windows and no more than 1% error rate increase.

If pilot passes we’ll attach language to the addendum that makes the SLO contingent on the pilot configuration — that’s standard. I’ll need a PO or a signed pilot statement (small fee to reserve burst nodes).

Attachments: SLA_Addendum_PulsePay_v2.pdf (draft), PulsePay_Q2_usage_summary.csv

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Operations, Redwood Inference
From: PulsePay Procurement <procure@pulsepay.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 04 Aug 2025 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Renewal conversation + premium SLA request / commercial questions

Karthik / Marissa,

Thanks — procurement reviewed the addendum. A couple of commercial asks before legal signs:

1) Term: prefer 12-month term but want a 30-day opt-out after 60 days if pilot shows unresolved performance regressions.
2) Credits: we want SLO credit calculation expressed as % refund to the monthly committed fee rather than a multiple of monthly credit.
3) Pricing: can you provide a final number for Option A (12m + burst)? We need it for our CFO approval.

If you can get back with numbers and a DocuSign-ready addendum by EOD Wednesday we’ll queue internal approvals.

Best,
Procurement team
PulsePay
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: PulsePay Procurement <procure@pulsepay.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 04 Aug 2025 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation + premium SLA request / commercial questions

Procurement — thanks for the specifics. Summary of what we’ll deliver by Wednesday EOD: 

- Finalized Option A commercial: 12-month commitment, dedicated baseline + 2x burst pool for up to 6 hours/day on 12 defined days/quarter. Fixed uplift: 22% on current committed run-rate. Line items included for pilot fee and onramp.
- Addendum edits: term language updated with a 60-day acceptance window and a 30-day exit option if the pilot fails to meet the agreed success criteria.
- Credit model: convert credits to a percentage refund tied to the monthly committed fee (we’ll propose 10% refund per qualifying SLO breach, capped at 40% per month).
- DocuSign link and an action checklist (pilot steps, PO, and timelines).

We’ll attach the updated SLA_Addendum_PulsePay_v2.pdf and send the DocuSign envelope for signature once you confirm the pricing.

Karthik
